result.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
result.summary: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. However, missing or inconsistent task information can obstruct teacher execution and weaken the resulting supervision. We propose WorkFactory, a scalable framework for constructing coherent and executable professional tasks. Starting from professional intents, information-level planning builds an information support graph to guide task instantiation, explicitly representing the dependencies and locations of information required for the intended outputs. Probe executions then identify support failures and guide repairs while preserving the intended work. We construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use the collected teacher trajectories to fine-tune Qwen models at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales, yielding the WorkPilot family. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling analyses reveal model-dependent diminishing returns, with execution length first increasing and then decreasing. Controlled component analyses show that planning and repair reduce probe-diagnosed task environment defects and improve downstream performance. The data and models are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 WorkFactory 框架，从职业意图出发用信息支撑图做信息层规划并实例化专业任务，再通过探针执行发现信息支撑失败并修复，构建 11 万余条任务与教师轨迹，微调出 WorkPilot 系列模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息支撑图 + 探针执行诊断—修复」流程可能可供核查：用于在生成答案前检验中间状态是否具备所需证据，或定位推理失败是信息缺失还是使用错误；但论文本身不涉及视觉或 latent 状态推理。
